why_this_file_exists: markdownEscape has ONE implementation (TypeScript), so it is not a shared/conformance corpus — those exist to keep several languages identical. It is table-driven anyway because it is the boundary between a scanned target's bytes and a document a person reads, and a table is auditable: a reviewer reads the cases, not the regexes. A case added here is a claim about what a target cannot do to a report.
value_forms: `value` is the JSON value passed to markdownEscape. Where JSON cannot express the input, `special` names it instead: undefined, nan, infinity, bigint, date, function. Exactly one of `out` (the expected string) or `throws` (a substring of the expected error message) is present.

structure.why: A value must not be able to write Markdown. These are the characters that would, each on its own, so a reviewer can see none is missing.

cases.why: the backslash is escaped exactly once, not twice: it is in the same regex pass as everything else
a backslash already escaping something stays one level deep
emphasis
code span
a code FENCE inside a value cannot open a block
a heading cannot start
a list cannot start
a link cannot form
an image cannot form
braces, for the templating languages downstream of a Markdown reader
angle brackets: autolinks and raw HTML both start with one
GFM strikethrough

table_breakout.why: Acceptance test 2. The pipe is the character a value most plausibly contains by accident — a shell pipeline, a regex alternation, a User-Agent — and the one that silently adds a column to somebody else's table.

cases.why: a pipe cannot end a cell
the test's own value: pipe, newline and emphasis land in ONE cell as text
a value that looks like a whole table row
a curl pipeline, the realistic case

html.why: Acceptance test 3. Escaping is the first of two defences; the pipeline also drops every html node after parsing. This section pins the first, so neither is load-bearing alone.

cases.why: the test's own payload becomes text
a script tag in a VALUE, as opposed to in a template
an HTML comment cannot open

line_breaks.why: There is no way to escape a line break in Markdown: a backslash before one IS a hard break, and inside a table row a raw newline ends the row. So a value cannot be allowed to carry one, and all three forms collapse to a single space.

cases.why: LF
CRLF becomes ONE space, not two: the pair is matched before the singles
bare CR, which an HTTP response line gives you
mixed endings in one value
a trailing newline does not become a hard break
two newlines cannot start a new paragraph

controls.why: An invisible difference between what a report says and what it contains is a lie about evidence. Tab becomes a space; every other C0 and DEL is removed. Inside a {% code %} block these same bytes SURVIVE and are shown as markers — that is evidence, and a different rule, in codeTag.ts.

cases.why: NUL is removed. A raw NUL in a text file makes grep call it binary and find nothing in it — this repo has already paid for that once, in packages/svelte/src/infra/load.ts
tab becomes a space, so it cannot be mistaken for cell alignment
BEL, ESC and the rest of C0 are removed
an ANSI escape sequence loses its ESC and reads as the text it is
vertical tab and form feed, which some renderers treat as line breaks
DEL is removed. §4.2 of the spec lists C0 only, §9.2 lists 'other C0 control characters and DEL': the two halves disagree and this follows the stricter one
a control character cannot sit between a backslash and the character it escapes

unicode_kept.why: Escaping must not become mangling. A report on a target in another script is still a report, and a finding whose bytes were altered on the way to the page is not evidence.

cases.why: CJK is untouched
an emoji with a zero-width joiner survives whole
combining marks are not separated from their base
a non-breaking space stays a non-breaking space: it is not C0

a right-to-left override is NOT removed today, and is listed so the decision is visible rather than absent. Trojan Source reordering inside a report is an open question for the ADR; recording current behaviour here means a change to it has to change a test

scalars.why: Numbers and booleans cannot carry Markdown, so they are stringified and not escaped. null and undefined are an author's 'nothing here' and print nothing — which is NOT the same as an unknown variable, already a render error by then under strictVariables.

cases.why: an integer
a negative number keeps its sign unescaped even though '-' is a special: String() of a number cannot produce Markdown
a float
true
false prints 'false', it does not vanish
null prints nothing
undefined prints nothing
NaN prints itself rather than an empty cell, which would read as a measurement of zero
Infinity likewise
a bigint, which JSON cannot hold but a count of bytes can reach
a Date renders ISO 8601 UTC rather than erroring, because a report full of timestamps should not need a filter
the empty string is empty, not absent

refused.why: A composite value is a TEMPLATE BUG, and a report that prints [object Object] has turned a bug into a finished document nobody can tell is wrong. The error names the shape and the fix, and never quotes the value: this message reaches a stored snapshot, a console page and every log on the way.

cases.why: an object: the author meant to pick a field
an array: the author meant to loop
an empty object is refused too — printing nothing would hide the bug
an empty array likewise
an array of rows, the realistic mistake: {{ result.price_changes }}
a function could only come from a context this module built, so it is named rather than coerced

size.why: Escaping never truncates. A value too large for a report is a size-cap decision made in render.ts against a stated limit, not a silent cut made here.

cases.why: a 100k-character value passes through, escaped, at full length
